Documentation section docs/exporting.md#Exporting > CSV:

`write_csv(books, path)` writes a header row and one row per book. Three columns
are written — title, author and ISBN — unless you pass `columns` yourself.

The chunk bookshelf/exporter.py::write_csv before the change:

def write_csv(books, path, columns=('title', 'author', 'isbn')):
    with open(path, 'w', newline='') as handle:
        writer = csv.writer(handle)
        writer.writerow(columns)
        for book in books:
            writer.writerow([getattr(book, column) for column in columns])

And after it:

def write_csv(books, path, columns=('title', 'author', 'isbn', 'year')):
    with open(path, 'w', newline='') as handle:
        writer = csv.writer(handle)
        writer.writerow(columns)
        for book in books:
            writer.writerow([getattr(book, column) for column in columns])
text: {"accurate":false,"explanation":"`write_csv` now writes four default columns (`title`, `author`, `isbn`, `year`), so the documentation’s claim that it writes only three unless `columns` is passed is no longer correct."}
